title: AppState heartbeat, version 1
description: The fixed record a containerised app publishes as its heartbeat and its own state (plan section 3.3 overlay sub-branch AppState; Phase 1 step 7; Phase 6 step 2 health check). The app writes each field as one leaf under its own sub-branch Vehicle.DualVm.AppState.<App> in the local databroker (<App> is derived from the manifest name by one rule: split on '-', upper-case the first letter of each part, join, so hard-brake-hazard gives HardBrakeHazard; names from the overlay draft, overlay.vspec); the twin connector assembles the leaves into this record, validates it against this schema, and forwards only a valid record (plan sections 3.2 and 3.8, S11). Design draft for Phase 0 step 6. Does NOT demonstrate: that any app runs, that the heartbeat is timely, or that an app cannot hide information in a permitted field -- the schema stops honest mistakes, not a malicious app (a boolean can carry one bit of anything). The data-flow proof is the Monitor-independence test in twin-allowlist.md.
$comment: HARD RULE (plan sections 3.2, 3.8, S11): no field of this record is derived, directly or indirectly, from the Vehicle.DualVm.Monitor branch or from anything else the QNX guest produces -- neither from the value of a Monitor leaf nor from its freshness or absence (a stale or missing Monitor value means the bridge is disconnected, which is guest connection state) -- no verdict, reason, count, MISS or RESTORED, bridge or guest connection state, guest time, catalogue-digest match, or profile. An app may read the Monitor branch to display the last verdict locally; that value, and whether it is fresh, never reaches any field below, and the app's decisions never take either as an input. Design values, each with its reason: (1) heartbeat period 1 s -- short enough that the Phase 6 health check sees several heartbeats inside any deadline of a few seconds, long enough to bound the app's heartbeat traffic; the health deadline itself is Phase 6's design value. (2) Every string is an enum or a tight pattern with maxLength, and there is no free-text field: a free-text 'message' field would be a ready channel for a verdict. (3) The record is flat (no objects, no arrays): the twin flattens it into dotted keys in the vss shadow, whose document is limited to 8 KB and 8 levels (F84). (4) Largest valid record, serialised: under 320 bytes. (5) No cross-field invariant exists: each field is true on its own at the moment it was written, so a record assembled from leaves delivered one by one (a 'torn' read across two heartbeats) is still correct field by field. (6) No timestamp field: freshness is judged by the observer on its own clock from seq changing; the databroker's datapoint timestamps (Linux host clock) exist anyway, and no guest time may appear. Annotations: 'x-vss-leaf' (the leaf under Vehicle.DualVm, whose name the overlay draft owns and overrides) and 'x-provenance' (where the value comes from; allowed values: app-build, updater-start, app-runtime) are not validation keywords; draft 2020-12 validators ignore them, and the pytest reads them. Changing this schema means a new $id version and a new const in schema_version; the old text is overwritten, not annotated.

propertyNames.$comment: Tripwire, coarse on purpose and failing closed (it would also block an innocent name such as transmission_mode or acceptance_level; rename such a field rather than loosen the list): with additionalProperties false an unknown name already fails; this makes a future edit that adds, say, last_verdict unusable, because every instance carrying it fails validation. The token list is lower-case only because the positive pattern already forces lower-case names (ECMA-262 regex has no inline case flag).

schema_version.$comment: A consumer (connector, updater, a later Athena query) must refuse a record whose version it does not know rather than guess at its fields. uint8 range is ample: a version changes only when the field set changes.

app.description: The app's name as its app-class entry in the local manifest (for example hard-brake-hazard).
app.$comment: The health check and the twin have to know which app is speaking. A pattern, not an enum, so that adding an app does not change this schema; the updater's health check compares it with the manifest entry it started, and the connector checks that it names the sub-branch the record came from (split on '-', upper-case the first letter of each part, join). 32 characters: longer than any proposed name, short enough to keep the record small; lower-case words of letters and digits joined by single hyphens, each word starting with a letter, so it is a name, cannot carry prose, and maps to exactly one sub-branch (a word starting with a digit would lose its hyphen in the mapping: x-1a and x1a would both give X1a). Same pattern as the manifest's name.

app_version.description: The app's own version, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, baked into the image at build time.
app_version.$comment: Image IDs differ per architecture (the PC's amd64 build and the arm64 builds on a1.metal and the Orin are different images), so the Phase 6 drill's v1 -> v2 -> v3 -> rollback sequence can only be compared across the three hosts through a label that is the same on all of them. Core semver only: pre-release and build suffixes are free text. Three digits per part is a design bound that no drill will reach.

image_id.description: The image ID (config digest) of the running container, passed in by whoever started it (the updater, or the dev loop by hand) as an environment variable at container start.
image_id.$comment: The Phase 6 health check has to attribute a heartbeat to the container it just started; without this field a still-running old container, or the databroker's retained last value of a dead one, could pass the check for the new one. A container cannot read its own image ID from inside without docker.sock, which no container ever has (plan section 3.7), so the starter injects it. The image ID is the cross-path pin the manifest uses (plan 1.2).

seq.description: Heartbeat counter: 1 at the first heartbeat after each container start, plus 1 at every heartbeat.
seq.$comment: The databroker keeps a signal's last value after its provider dies, so a present AppState proves nothing; a seq that keeps changing, judged on the observer's own clock, does. A seq that goes back marks a restart. uint32 at the 1 s period lasts about 136 years, so no wrap handling is needed. Recommendation to the connector: a change of seq alone should not drive a vss shadow update (send it with the next other change, or at most once per 60 s): the send cadence bounds shadow traffic while keeping the counter available with the next state change.

state.description: The app's own lifecycle state, computed from its own process and its own non-Monitor VSS inputs; never from the value or freshness of the Monitor branch. starting: connected to the databroker, subscriptions not yet serving values. running: serving. degraded: running, but one of its own non-Monitor VSS inputs (for hard-brake-hazard: Vehicle.DualVm.Motion.LongitudinalVelocity and Vehicle.Acceleration.Longitudinal) is missing or older than the app's own input deadline, or its last Actuate, if any, did not return ok. stopping: termination requested.
state.$comment: The health check needs 'running'; 'degraded' lets a deliberately broken v3 show itself as broken rather than as dead. A Monitor value that is absent or stale (the bridge disconnected) is guest connection state, so it must never make the app 'degraded': test A8's absent-Monitor arm checks exactly that. An enum, because a free-text status is a channel.
state.x-vss-leaf: AppState.<App>.State (sensor, string, allowed: starting, running, degraded, stopping)

hazard_requested.description: The value the app last requested through Actuate on Vehicle.Body.Lights.Hazard.IsSignaling; false if it has requested nothing since start.
hazard_requested.$comment: The app's own output (Phase 1 step 7), decided from two inputs only: the signed Vehicle.DualVm.Motion.LongitudinalVelocity and Vehicle.Acceleration.Longitudinal. Deceleration along the direction of travel is minus a_x times the sign of the velocity (overlay.vspec, Acceleration.Longitudinal): Vehicle.Speed is |v_x|, so an app using it could not tell braking in reverse (positive a_x) from accelerating forward. Set beside the allowlisted current value of IsSignaling, it shows whether the actuation path followed the app. Never decided or overridden from the Monitor branch.

actuate_result.description: Outcome of the app's last Actuate call. none: no Actuate since start. ok: accepted. unavailable: the databroker reported that no provider serves the actuator (F19). error: any other failure.
actuate_result.$comment: Distinguishes 'the app decided but the actuation path is absent' from 'the app never decided'. An enum, because a gRPC error text is free text and could carry anything the Linux side has seen.
actuate_result.x-vss-leaf: AppState.<App>.ActuateResult (sensor, string, allowed: none, ok, unavailable, error)
